structured_output.world_model:
W2 (empirical), after E053. Tip E049: 5.198 s, 0.7535 on seeds 0-2. Same code rerun (E050) gave 5.206 s and 0.7552. E053 (group-2 freeze moved from 90% to 85%) gave 5.075 s and 0.7562, so about -0.12 s with no visible accuracy loss. That is consistent with about 10 ms saved per frozen step, and it means group 2 has no cliff at this dose. Rebuild noise is about 0.3 pp on a 3-seed mean and about ±0.03 s on time. The population mean is about 0.752, so headroom over the 0.75 bar is about 0.2 pp.

Mechanisms, with support:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch for 0.0-0.25 pp, roughly 1.5-2 s/pp (E020, E023, E027, E049).
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, confounded, E006) are already in the tip. More than 10 time-neutral boosters were flat or negative (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, wd, LS). Optimizer, averaging and regularization are flat within about 0.2 pp.
3. Time tracks pixels. Early 20 px is nearly free (E026, E033). Trimming steps or samples costs about as much as the dial (E031, E040, E041, E045, E048). E052 stacked selection with a top-up and was slightly better than the dial, within noise.
4. Backward truncation is the best lever (E028, E034, E036, E046, E049, E053). It is bandwidth-heavy. Freezing group 1 at 60% is a cliff (E037, -0.38 pp), so there is a 32 px adaptation requirement for the stem. E039 and E042 saved only 0.03-0.05 s.
5. Architecture cuts cost accuracy at the dial's rate or worse (E010, E021, E051).
6. Non-step overhead is about 2.5% (E047). Systems work recovers at most about 1% (E035).
7. Noise: a rebuild alone moves the 3-seed mean by 0.3 pp, so differences under 0.3 pp on seeds 0-2 are not resolvable. The kept tip is probably a lucky draw.

Misses: I under-predicted the savings of cuts and selection (E046, E048, E052). I over-predicted time-neutral boosters. For E053 I predicted accuracy too low, since a larger freeze dose did not hurt.

Unsure:
- Whether the intermittent stem backward keeps accuracy. The E037 cliff suggests stem updates matter, but the 28 px phase is not the 32 px phase.
- Whether ReLU saves 3% or more. I expect 1-3%.
- How far the group-2 freeze can go before a cliff.

forecasts.reason: Half of 71 steps at about 7 ms saved each gives about 0.25 s at best; accuracy risk is moderate because E037 showed the stem needs updates, but the 28 px phase is milder.
The 4% extra frozen steps (about 9) save about 0.07 s; accuracy is probably flat to slightly lower, below the noise floor.
The offline profile will likely project a saving under 3%, so the idea closes with no run; if a run happens, the numbers stay near the tip.
The stacked cuts save about 0.2-0.3 s and the top-up costs about 0.1 s, so time falls about 3%; accuracy sits at the noise-limited tip level.

cruxes: Does the intermittent 28 px stem backward keep accuracy within 0.1 pp? This sets whether the stem updates are needed every step or only occasionally.
Is there a group-2 freeze cliff between the 85% start and an earlier one? E053 suggests none yet, and each frozen step saves about 10 ms.
Does ReLU's backward save at least 3% in Inductor? If so, it is a free per-step cut.
